description: Batches a decoder rejects alone, each breaking one rule of ledgers.md section 7, or two where its name says so, with the reason code of the first rule a decoder checks; every batch long enough to hold one carries the CRC-32C of its bytes, but the crc-mismatch case.

cases.name: No bytes.
The fixed header and three bytes, one short of the CRC-32C.
Magic XLLB.
Version 2.
A CRC-32C which does not match the bytes.
Flags 0x81: the start flag and bit 7.
A segment offset of 0 in two bytes, 0x80 0x00, longer than its shortest form.
A segment offset of 11 bytes, whose 10th byte carries past the u64.
A row count which reaches the CRC-32C unterminated: a header varint is bad-varint there.
The start flag with segment offset 1.
No start flag, with segment offset 0.
The start flag with ordinal base 1.
No start flag and no rows: only a marker holds none.
One counted row and no row bytes.
A defining row whose key runs one byte past the CRC-32C.
A referencing row whose ordinal reaches the CRC-32C unterminated: a row's varint is row-truncated there.
A body whose length runs one byte past the CRC-32C.
A row of kind 3.
A row with bit 3 set.
A body length of 0 in two bytes, longer than its shortest form.
A defining row with an empty key.
A defining row whose key length is 65,536.
A version base of 33 bytes.
A token of 33 bytes.
A batch which starts a segment and references ordinal 0 before defining any key.
Ordinal base 2 and a reference to ordinal 2, which no row before it defined.
A byte between the last counted row and the CRC-32C.
Flags 0x02, without the start flag, and segment offset 0, which breaks bad-segment-offset too: bad-flags comes first.
No rows without the start flag, and trailing bytes: no-rows comes first.
A row of kind 3 with an empty key: bad-row-flags comes first.
